cards.notes: Reserve a free general-admission ticket for galleries, then allow time for the Sculpture Gardens at 10 Art Museum Drive near North Charles Street.
cards.short_summary: Free general-admission art museum near the North Charles corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Baltimore Museum of Art is at 10 Art Museum Drive near North Charles Street, and general admission is free.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Baltimore Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Free general-admission tickets are required; special exhibitions need separate tickets.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten recurring Loyola University Maryland traditions documented by the university, spanning campus culture, scholarship, service, music, faith, and athletics.

cards.title: Begin the spring term with the MLK Convocation
cards.subtitle: Annual January community convocation
cards.notes: Look for the annual January program and use it as a focused way to join Loyola’s public inquiry into race, justice, politics, and spirituality.
cards.short_summary: A Loyola-wide January gathering centered on issues of racial justice and public life.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola describes MLK Convocation as an annual January gathering for shared inquiry into social justice, politics, spirituality, and the legacies of race and racial justice in America.
cards.source_title: School Spirit and Traditions | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: Check Loyola’s event listings for the current year’s program details.

cards.title: Wear green and grey for the Battle of Charles Street
cards.subtitle: Annual Loyola–Johns Hopkins lacrosse matchup
cards.notes: Follow the scheduled lacrosse matchup with Johns Hopkins and experience the rivalry in the stands alongside the Greyhound community.
cards.short_summary: The annual lacrosse meeting between Loyola and nearby rival Johns Hopkins.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola identifies the Battle of Charles Street as its annual lacrosse matchup against long-time local rival Johns Hopkins University.
cards.source_title: School Spirit and Traditions | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: Consult the current Loyola Athletics schedule and ticket information before attending.

cards.title: Catch the campus-scale energy of Loyolapalooza
cards.subtitle: Annual spring festival and concert
cards.notes: Watch for spring announcements, then plan around the concert and festival programming; the Battle of the Bands winner opens the show.
cards.short_summary: A spring festival that combines rides, food, activities, and a headline concert on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola says its annual springtime Loyolapalooza brings carnival rides, food, fun, and a concert to campus, opened by the Battle of the Bands winner.
cards.source_title: School Spirit and Traditions | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: Programming and attendance details vary by year; check Student Leadership and Involvement announcements.

cards.title: See the BSA Fashion Show take the stage
cards.subtitle: Black Student Association cultural showcase
cards.notes: Look for the Black Student Association’s event details and attend the show to support a campus celebration of Black culture and talent.
cards.short_summary: A fashion, music, and community event organized by Loyola’s Black Student Association.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola describes the BSA Fashion Show as a highly anticipated Black Student Association event celebrating Black culture and talent through fashion, music, and community.
cards.source_title: School Spirit and Traditions | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: Check the Black Student Association or campus events calendar for current presentation details.

cards.title: Mark graduation season at Senior Soiree
cards.subtitle: Senior-class celebration before Commencement
cards.notes: Eligible seniors can watch for class communications and use the evening to celebrate together before the Commencement ceremony.
cards.short_summary: A formal senior-class gathering with dinner, dancing, and a pre-Commencement sendoff.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola identifies Senior Soiree as a senior-class gathering under a tent on the President’s Lawn for dinner, dancing, and celebration before Commencement.
cards.source_title: School Spirit and Traditions | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: This event is for the graduating senior class; consult senior-class communications for participation details.

cards.title: Open the year at the Mass of the Holy Spirit
cards.subtitle: Early-September gathering in Alumni Memorial Chapel
cards.notes: In early September, join the Loyola community in Alumni Memorial Chapel for music, song, and prayer for the academic year ahead.
cards.short_summary: Loyola’s opening-of-year Mass, connected to a Jesuit educational tradition dating to 1548.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola says the community gathers at the Mass of the Holy Spirit early each September and traces the tradition to the first Jesuit school in Messina, Sicily, in 1548.
cards.source_title: School Spirit and Traditions | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: Held early in September; verify the current academic-year date and chapel details through Loyola events.

cards.title: Reconnect during Initium Week
cards.subtitle: Annual fall return-to-campus week
cards.notes: Use the fall schedule to pick a concert, game, tournament, or the Student Activities Fair as a low-pressure way to reconnect on campus.
cards.short_summary: A fall week of events welcoming students back to campus and community.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola describes Initium Week as a fall return-to-campus week with events to reconnect, including concerts, games, a beach volleyball tournament, and the Fall Student Activities Fair.
cards.source_title: School Spirit and Traditions | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: Review the current Initium Week calendar and select individual events that fit your schedule.

cards.title: Hear the Belles and Chimes at Chordbusters
cards.subtitle: Twice-yearly a cappella concert
cards.notes: Plan ahead when ticket information is released for this twice-yearly concert featuring Loyola’s Belles and Chimes a cappella groups.
cards.short_summary: A recurring Loyola a cappella showcase with the Belles and Chimes.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola identifies Chordbusters as a twice-a-year a cappella concert and reports that the Belles and Chimes have performed it together since 1986.
cards.access_notes: Ticket availability can be limited; use the current event announcement for timing and access information.

cards.title: Follow a text through the Humanities Symposium
cards.subtitle: Week-long liberal-arts event series
cards.notes: Check the featured text and event lineup, then choose a session that connects students, faculty, friends of Loyola, and Baltimore participants.
cards.short_summary: A week-long series of events centered on a selected text and Loyola’s liberal-arts heritage.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola describes the Humanities Symposium as a week-long series of events related to a particular text for students, faculty, friends of the University, and the Baltimore community.
cards.source_title: School Spirit and Traditions | Loyola University Maryland
cards.access_notes: The featured text and individual sessions change by year; consult the current symposium schedule.

cards.title: Share candlelight and song at Lessons & Carols
cards.subtitle: Seasonal service in Alumni Memorial Chapel
cards.notes: Arrive with enough time for a chapel service that combines candlelight and Christmas carols during Loyola’s Advent and Christmas season.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal Loyola chapel service of candlelight, carols, and scripture.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola identifies Lessons & Carols as a seasonal service in Alumni Memorial Chapel featuring candlelight and Christmas carols; Loyola Magazine reports the tradition has brought campus together since 1988.
cards.access_notes: Verify the current seasonal date and chapel entry details through Loyola’s events calendar.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Loyola University Maryland, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-key, under-21-safe first-weekend loop: orient yourself, find a few useful campus landmarks, then end with a current student-program option.

cards.title: Start with the Evergreen Campus map
cards.subtitle: Orientation stop · Loyola’s Evergreen Campus
cards.notes: Save the official campus map, then use it to locate campus buildings, shuttle stops, dining, and the pedestrian bridge before heading out.
cards.short_summary: Get your bearings with Loyola’s official map first.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola’s official campus map identifies the Evergreen Campus and its named buildings, services, shuttle stops, and visitor parking.
cards.access_notes: The Evergreen Campus is open to visitors during regular business hours; academic and administrative facilities are locked after hours.

cards.title: Walk the Academic Quad
cards.subtitle: Orientation stop · Evergreen Campus
cards.notes: Use the quad as your daytime route between academic buildings. Pause to identify nearby landmarks so future meetups need less map-checking.
cards.short_summary: Make the central campus walk familiar.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola describes walking across the Quad as part of the Evergreen Campus experience and documents the Quad among campus scenes.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus area; follow posted campus-access guidance.

cards.title: Cross the USF&G Pedestrian Bridge
cards.subtitle: Orientation stop · Across North Charles Street
cards.notes: Take the marked bridge once in daylight to connect the two sides of campus, then note the buildings and services immediately beyond it.
cards.short_summary: Learn the safe campus crossing over North Charles.
cards.evidence_claim: The official campus map identifies the USF&G Pedestrian Bridge, and Loyola describes a pedestrian bridge crossing North Charles Street.
cards.access_notes: Use the designated pedestrian bridge and observe campus safety guidance.

cards.title: Find the Loyola/Notre Dame Library
cards.subtitle: Study-planning stop · East side of campus
cards.notes: Locate the library entrance now, then return when you need a quiet place to begin an assignment or meet a classmate to study.
cards.short_summary: Put the shared campus library on your mental map.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola identifies the Loyola/Notre Dame Library as serving Loyola, Notre Dame of Maryland University, and the surrounding community on the east side of campus.
cards.access_notes: Check the library directly for current building and service hours.

cards.title: See what’s on at the Julio Fine Arts Gallery
cards.subtitle: Culture stop · DeChiaro College Center
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition and gallery hours, then take a short gallery visit between campus stops. Events are listed as free and open to the public.
cards.short_summary: A compact on-campus art stop with changing exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Julio Fine Arts Gallery is in the DeChiaro College Center, holds exhibitions and a permanent collection, and states that all gallery events are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Current page lists weekday gallery hours; confirm the exhibition schedule before going.

cards.title: Pause at Alumni Memorial Chapel
cards.subtitle: Reflection stop · West side of the Academic Quad
cards.notes: Walk by the chapel and its stained glass, or attend a scheduled service if that suits you. Use the accessible south-end entrance when needed.
cards.short_summary: A landmark for reflection, architecture, and scheduled worship.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola locates Alumni Memorial Chapel on the west side of the Academic Quad and documents its Gothic Revival design and dedication to alumni lost in World Wars I and II.
cards.access_notes: The chapel has an accessible, level entrance at its south end; consult Campus Ministry for service details.

cards.title: Plan a meal at Boulder Garden Café
cards.subtitle: Meal stop · Andrew White Student Center
cards.notes: Check the menu and choose a breakfast, lunch, dinner, or weekend brunch window that works with your plan and dietary needs.
cards.short_summary: A campus dining stop with breakfast, lunch, dinner, and weekend brunch.
cards.evidence_claim: Boulder Garden Café is located in the Andrew White Student Center and offers breakfast, lunch, dinner, plus all-you-care-to-eat weekend brunch and dinner service.
cards.access_notes: The café accepts meal-plan options, Evergreen dollars, cash, and credit cards; check the dining page for current menus and hours.

cards.title: Find Reitz Arena before an event
cards.subtitle: Campus-event stop · Forbes Court
cards.notes: Locate the arena and check Loyola Athletics or campus events for a scheduled basketball, volleyball, concert, or university gathering you can attend.
cards.short_summary: Know where Loyola’s arena events take place.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola states that Reitz Arena hosts basketball and volleyball games and also serves as an auditorium, concert venue, and liturgical space.
cards.access_notes: Event access, timing, and any ticket requirements vary; verify the specific event before traveling.

cards.title: Take a daylight walk to the FAC
cards.subtitle: Wellness stop · 4900 N. Charles Street
cards.notes: Bring your Loyola ID, confirm facility hours, and pick one low-pressure option—track, pool, climbing wall, or a group exercise class—to try later.
cards.short_summary: Set up an easy recreation option near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola’s Fitness & Aquatic Center includes aquatics, fitness, activity courts, a climbing wall, exercise studios, a jogging track, and outdoor playing fields; full-time undergraduates have automatic membership.
cards.access_notes: A short walk or shuttle ride from main campus; hours, pool hours, rock-wall hours, and class schedules can vary.

cards.title: Check the Late Night listing
cards.subtitle: Evening activity stop · Loyola campus
cards.notes: Look for the current student-event listing and choose an activity that fits your Friday or Saturday. Bring a friend or use it as an easy introduction.
cards.short_summary: A recurring campus option for Thursday, Friday, and Saturday nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Loyola’s International Student Services resource page states that the Late Night program plans events and activities every Thursday, Friday, and Saturday night during the academic year.
cards.access_notes: Late Night is documented for Thursday, Friday, and Saturday nights during the academic year; confirm the current listing, venue, and start time.
